messages:
maria.finance: FYI I just reported a phishing email I got — had a 'view document' link that went to a weird consent page asking to connect my Google account. I clicked and approved before I realized. ugh.
sec-bot: Ticket created: SEC-2026-987. Assigned to @ravi. Please confirm if credentials were entered or just OAuth consent granted. :rotating_light:
ravi: Thanks @maria.finance. Short Qs: did the flow ask for username/password or did it open an OAuth consent screen listing scopes? If you remember scope names that helps (drive, gmail, profile, etc).
maria.finance: It showed a Google-like consent modal — said "Redwood Docs Viewer wants to: View and manage the files in your Google Drive". I clicked allow. I did NOT type my password, only clicked allow.
anya: Uploaded the email + headers to sandbox. Initial automated analysis: attachment was HTML redirect to an oauth phishing host: docs-viewer[dot]info -> then JS opened OAuth popup to accounts.google.com with forged-looking params. No binary payload detected.
anya: Sandbox paste and headers:
```
From: "Redwood Billing" <billing@redwood-pay[.]com>
Subject: New invoice for March
Received-SPF: neutral (docs-viewer[.]info)
Links: https://docs-viewer.info/view?d=0x88a...
Embedded JS: window.open('https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https://docs-viewer.info/cb')
```
ravi: Ok — this is an OAuth consent phishing where the attacker used a third-party app to get Drive scopes. Containment plan:
- Immediately revoke the OAuth grant for maria.finance
- Block docs-viewer.info at proxy/firewall and add to blocklist
- Search logs for tokens issued and app client_id usage
- Rotate service accounts if any were used
- Notify Legal & Privacy if any sensitive Drive folders were accessible
jordan: Adding: check Cloud Audit logs for tokens.exchange and Drive activity from the user around 2026-03-07T10:10Z -> 2026-03-07T10:30Z. Also check SSA (shared folder) changes and external share grants.
ravi: Maria — do NOT re-login to Google from that tab. Go to myaccount.google.com -> Security -> Third-party apps with account access and revoke the app named "Redwood Docs Viewer" or anything unknown. I'll also revoke sessions from admin console.
maria.finance: Done — I revoked the app and removed the session. I also changed nothing else yet.
anya: SIEM query (Splunk) to surface related activity:
```
index=cloud logs (event_type="oauth.token.issue" OR event_type="drive.file.create") client_id="<attacker_client_id>" OR url=*docs-viewer.info* | stats count by user,client_id,src_ip
```
anya: Sandbox also captured the OAuth client_id: 104123-attackid.apps.googleusercontent.com. Adding to IOCs.
ravi: Running revocation from admin API now (sample command):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  "https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/maria.finance@redwood.com/tokens/104123-attackid.apps.googleusercontent.com:revoke"
```
ravi: After revocation, check Drive file export logs and DLP alerts for large downloads or external grant creations. If we see lateral movement, escalate to incident response and Legal.
legal: Please capture a timeline and list of potentially accessed resources. We may need to notify customers if PHI/PII is confirmed exfiltrated.
anya: Quick hit: SIEM shows one token exchange for maria.finance from src_ip 18.204.12.33 at 2026-03-07T10:12Z and a Drive file read event shortly after (drive.files.get) for a doc in a marketing shared drive. No mass downloads seen in first 20m. Continuing scan.
ops-oncall (bot): Block rule applied to firewall for docs-viewer.info by ravi at 2026-03-07T10:20Z. Proxy will deny traffic to that host.
ravi: Good. Next steps:
- Confirm revocation succeeded (admin console + user page)
- Run a full Drive audit for the user and for any files the attacker accessed
- Pull file metadata for external sharing/grants since 2026-03-01
- Security will draft an internal heads-up to Sales + Finance to watch for similar emails
- Schedule a 30-min post-incident stand to capture action items
maria.finance: Thanks all. I'd like a HR/awareness note too — I forwarded the original email to phish@redwood.com per guidelines but I wasn't sure what to do after I clicked allow.
ravi: We'll include a short reminder in the team Slack and schedule a micro-training. Also prep a short FAQ about how OAuth consent phishing looks.
jordan: I'll create a follow-up ticket to add docs-viewer.info to the blocklist and add the attacker client_id to the OAuth denylist. Also suggestion: enable "Block third-party app access to sensitive scopes" policy for GSuite org.
anya: No signs of wide compromise so far. Marking incident as P1 -> Active monitoring. Will update SEC-2026-987 with full timeline and sandbox artifacts.
sec-bot: Ticket SEC-2026-987 updated: containment: revocation + domain block; detection: SIEM token exchange + drive read; status: monitoring. Assigned to @ravi and @anya. :white_check_mark:
maria.finance: Appreciate the quick help. Let me know if I need to do anything else (password change? MFA?)
ravi: Password change not strictly needed since creds weren't phished, but rotate refresh tokens for apps and enforce MFA if not already. We can advise a password rotation if any doubt. We'll follow up with Legal/Privacy if Drive content is sensitive.
